concepts.name: Celestial Objects and Their Types
concepts.summary: Name and distinguish stars, planets, moons, asteroids, comets and galaxies.

concepts.name: Earth's Rotation and Day
concepts.summary: Explain that Earth's spin on its axis causes day and night and the apparent daily motion of the sky.

concepts.name: Earth's Orbit and Seasons
concepts.summary: Explain that seasons result from Earth's axial tilt as it orbits the Sun, not from distance.

concepts.name: Phases of the Moon
concepts.summary: Describe the monthly cycle of lunar phases as changing views of the Moon's sunlit half.

concepts.name: Planets of the Solar System
concepts.summary: Recall the eight planets in order from the Sun and group them as rocky or giant.

concepts.name: Stars as Distant Suns
concepts.summary: Understand that stars are self-luminous balls of gas like the Sun, appearing faint because of great distance.

concepts.name: Constellations and Navigation
concepts.summary: Recognise that constellations are apparent patterns and use a few, such as the Big Dipper, to find Polaris.

misconceptions.text: Seasons happen because Earth is closer to the Sun in summer and farther in winter.
The phases of the Moon are caused by Earth's shadow falling on it.
Stars in a constellation are all close together in space.

concepts.name: Eclipses of Sun and Moon
concepts.summary: Use the alignment of Sun, Earth and Moon and the tilted lunar orbit to explain when each eclipse type occurs.

concepts.name: Tides and the Moon
concepts.summary: Explain how the Moon's gravity produces two tidal bulges and spring and neap tides.

concepts.name: Gravity Governing Orbits
concepts.summary: Use gravity's dependence on mass and distance to explain why bodies orbit and how orbital speed varies.

concepts.name: Kepler's Laws of Motion
concepts.summary: Apply the ideas that orbits are ellipses, that planets speed up nearer the Sun, and that farther planets take longer to orbit.

concepts.name: Light-Years and Cosmic Distances
concepts.summary: Convert and compare distances in astronomical units and light-years, and see that looking far means looking back in time.

concepts.name: Stellar Brightness and Colour
concepts.summary: Relate a star's colour to its temperature and distinguish apparent brightness from true luminosity.

concepts.name: Telescope Types and Light Gathering
concepts.summary: Explain that telescopes mainly gather light, and compare refracting and reflecting designs.

misconceptions.text: Astronauts float on the space station because there is no gravity there.
A telescope's main job is to magnify, so higher magnification is always better.
A brighter-looking star must be physically more luminous than a dimmer one.

concepts.name: Electromagnetic Spectrum in Astronomy
concepts.summary: Match wavelength bands to the objects and processes they reveal and why some need space telescopes.

concepts.name: Stellar Spectra and Composition
concepts.summary: Interpret absorption and emission lines to infer a star's composition and temperature.

concepts.name: Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram
concepts.summary: Analyse where stars fall by luminosity and temperature and what the main sequence, giants and white dwarfs represent.

concepts.name: Doppler Shift and Radial Velocity
concepts.summary: Use shifts in spectral lines to determine motion toward or away from us.

concepts.name: Stellar Parallax Distances
concepts.summary: Calculate distances to nearby stars from their apparent shift as Earth orbits, in parsecs.

concepts.name: Nuclear Fusion in Stars
concepts.summary: Explain how hydrogen fusion powers stars and how hydrostatic balance sets their stability.

concepts.name: Stellar Life Cycle by Mass
concepts.summary: Compare the evolution of low-mass and high-mass stars from nebula to white dwarf, neutron star or black hole.

concepts.name: Exoplanet Detection Methods
concepts.summary: Analyse how transit and radial-velocity methods find planets and what biases each carries.

misconceptions.text: Stars on the HR diagram move along the main sequence as they age like a path through life.
Stars burn fuel by chemical combustion like a fire.
Redshift means an object is red or that it is hot.

concepts.name: Mass-Luminosity and Stellar Lifetimes
concepts.summary: Evaluate why massive stars are far more luminous yet live much shorter lives than low-mass stars.

concepts.name: Cosmic Distance Ladder
concepts.summary: Evaluate how parallax, Cepheids and Type Ia supernovae chain together and where uncertainties accumulate.

concepts.name: Galaxy Types and Structure
concepts.summary: Analyse differences between spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies and the Milky Way's components.

concepts.name: Dark Matter Evidence
concepts.summary: Assess evidence from rotation curves, lensing and cluster dynamics for unseen mass and alternative explanations.

concepts.name: Hubble's Law and Expansion
concepts.summary: Interpret the redshift-distance relation as space expanding and estimate the age scale from the Hubble constant.

concepts.name: Big Bang Evidence
concepts.summary: Evaluate how the CMB, light-element abundances and expansion jointly support the Big Bang model.

concepts.name: Compact Objects and Black Holes
concepts.summary: Analyse the properties of white dwarfs, neutron stars and black holes, including event horizons and how they are detected.

concepts.name: Planetary System Formation
concepts.summary: Analyse how accretion in a protoplanetary disk explains planet types, orbits and observed exoplanet systems.

misconceptions.text: The Big Bang was an explosion at a point in space into empty space.
Black holes act like cosmic vacuum cleaners that suck in everything nearby.
Distant galaxies are moving away because they are flying through space from a central point.

concepts.name: Hubble Tension Assessment
concepts.summary: Critique why local distance-ladder and CMB-based values of the Hubble constant disagree and what resolutions are proposed.

concepts.name: Dark Energy and Cosmic Fate
concepts.summary: Evaluate evidence for accelerating expansion and compare scenarios for the universe's long-term future.

concepts.name: Inflation and Structure Origin
concepts.summary: Evaluate how inflation addresses the horizon and flatness problems and seeds structure seen in CMB fluctuations.

concepts.name: Gravitational Wave Astronomy
concepts.summary: Judge what gravitational-wave signals from mergers reveal that light cannot, including multi-messenger cases.

concepts.name: Galaxy and Black Hole Coevolution
concepts.summary: Evaluate how mergers, feedback and supermassive black holes shape galaxy growth in a dark-matter framework.

concepts.name: Designing Observational Programs
concepts.summary: Design an observation plan choosing instruments, wavelengths, sampling and controls to test a specific astrophysical question.

concepts.name: Biosignature and Habitability Assessment
concepts.summary: Construct a case for a planet's habitability from atmospheric, orbital and stellar data while weighing false positives.

misconceptions.text: Dark energy and dark matter are the same unseen thing acting in different ways.
Inflation is simply the Big Bang's expansion and is fully confirmed as a theory.
Detecting a single gas such as oxygen in an exoplanet atmosphere proves life exists there.
